justification: Vote 1, native read-aloud of the whole unit, read straight through and cold before any diff was opened: title, five paragraphs, five prompts, twenty options, five rationales; then the fleet-repair-3 regions (q5 A/B/C, the whole q5 rationale, q3-A, q3-B and the q3-B rationale sentence, q3's final clause, q1-C) re-read in their new surroundings. ALL FIVE r3 FINDINGS ARE DISCHARGED IN THE LIVE TEXT (they survive only inside generator_meta.repair_log, which no learner sees). (1) The r3 KILL is gone with the sentence that carried it: 'the one the writer says the stamps ...' does not occur in any live layer in any form, and every relative in the replacement rationale has a gap – 'the grievance a reader supplies unprompted', 'the line that baits this option', 'the argument the text is having', 'a limb the text supports', 'a limb the text refuses', 'the sentence she raised herself', 'the July draft that carries'. I re-gapped every zero relative in the unit as well and all thirteen bind: 'the same width it always was', 'the hinged ramp the vehicles drive over', 'the only measure the contract knows', 'something nobody asks her about', 'the reading she prefers', 'the cause she assigns them', 'a spacing it did not have', 'a locking sequence he lists', 'the interval Cottam gives'. No new gapless relative anywhere. (2) The r3 minor on q1-C is discharged and the fix is sound rather than merely different: 'one quarter during the past six years' has no partitive, so the eighteen-months fraction reading is unreachable; the stacked adverbials ('in one quarter' specific, 'during the past six years' framing) are the ordinary English pattern ('it rained on one day during the past six weeks'), so the one-word change buys the fix without buying awkwardness. The q1 rationale's paraphrase, 'one quarter unpaid in six years', still describes the option it faces. (3) The r3 comma-splice minor is discharged: the spliced sentence is gone and its replacement subordinates with 'since' ('Its first limb is true in the plainest way, since the reliability figure tells one story about the crossing and the ticket stamps tell another'). I swept the unit for splices independently and found none: the two long comma-runs (paragraph 2's 'The booked crossing sets ..., the round trip sets ..., and a passenger waits ...' and q4's colon-enumeration 'where her case thins is the join, her thirteen years hold ..., she says herself ..., and the timetable is ...') are both licensed serial coordinations closing on 'and', not splices. (4) The r3 major pronoun reach went with the same sentence. (5) q3's 'began it' is now 'what first stretched the gap between departures' – the pronoun is gone rather than re-aimed, and the clause echoes option C's own wording, which is the better repair. PASSAGE: clean, and I would not touch a word of it. The three quoted voices read as speech and not as composed prose – six quoted spans, six contractions across all three speakers, and the two uncontracted spans ('Two boats and the old book gave you a departure every twenty-five minutes' / 'and nobody writes to me about it') have no natural contraction site. The 'else' echo ('Something else happened in the middle of my series' -> 'says the something else is nearly the whole of it') still lands. WHAT I CONVICT is in the q4 rationale and is pre-existing, missed by r1, r2 and r3, recorded above; it is a flag, not a kill, because the quotation marks let a reader recover the mention reading, but it stumbles the ear. CONSIDERED AND CLEARED, so the next round does not churn them: (a) q5 rationale 'and that silence, rather than any difference of confidence, is what separates it from D' – 'it' is A, twenty-four words back, but the frame 'separates X from D' forces X to be an option letter and 'that silence' is already the subject, so nothing competes; this is NOT the r3 major recurring, where 'it' opened a fresh clause after a semicolon with no licensor at all. (b) q5-B 'a set of ticket stamps that tell different stories' – the plural relative takes the whole coordination, which 'different stories' independently forces. (c) q3 rationale 'arithmetic the text supplies but never adds up' – the shared object gap survives the intransitive 'add up' reading. (d) Cattermay's 'Something else happened in the middle of my series that I can’t take apart yet' – an extraposed relative over a short PP, normal in speech, and both available antecedents point the same way. RECORDED, OUT OF THIS GATE'S REMIT, for the integrated read: the q2 rationale still calls option C 'a HEDGED DISTRACTOR' and 'the unit’s second break of the correct-equals-qualified correlation', but the option it now faces ('It made no allowance for loading, which took longer then than it does now') carries no hedge at all; the rest of that note, including 'C’s relative clause runs the other way', does describe the current option. And q5's 'with a soft place found in each principal’s arithmetic' over-reaches: paragraph 5 finds a soft place in Cattermay's join and in Cottam's decade, but nothing in Bexwarden's arithmetic. Neither is a language defect and neither is convicted here.

findings: so the ramp did not put the second boat off the run -> so the ramp did not take the second boat off the run (q3 rationale, final clause of the B note – flag, GARDEN PATH / wrong collocation, PRE-EXISTING: the English idiom for withdrawing a vessel from a service is 'take X off the run'; 'put X off' is a very high-frequency phrasal verb meaning postpone or deter, so 'did not put the second boat off' is parsed as 'did not deter the second boat' until the reader reaches 'the run' and reparses. 'take' is the verb the collocation wants and removes the false phrasal reading; one verb changes, nothing else moves)
justification: Vote 2, systematic sweep of the failure classes that have actually shipped in this pipeline, run over all four live layers and not only the changed spans. PREPOSITION CALQUES: none. Checked and correct – 'berth within ten minutes of', 'asked ... for something narrow', 'went at it from the passenger’s end', 'penalised for altering', 'lost forty-one sailings to weather and a gearbox', 'goes out to tender', 'ranked getting across sooner below knowing when the boat would go', 'turns on how far behind', 'made no allowance for', 'had more to do with X than with Y' (parallel 'with' on both arms), 'removed more departures from the day', 'go into the next one', 'a dispute over which of them to believe', 'the disagreement over what connects the two', 'the argument over whether', 'says nothing that joins the ramp to the boat', 'dock an operator for cancellations', 'leaves the count altogether', 'stand behind them in any room'. The one collocation failure in this class is convicted above. COUNTABILITY: 'work that really has got longer' and 'arithmetic the text supplies' are correctly mass; 'some of the frequency' is deliberate; 'The fifteen minutes are real' (individuated, plural) against 'The ninety seconds is a manufacturer’s figure' (a measurement, singular) is right in both places. FALSE FRIENDS: none – 'concede', 'volunteers', 'in terms', and 'principal' (the party, correctly spelled, not 'principle') are all in their English senses. ARTICLE MISUSE: no Swedish zero article anywhere; the bare idioms ('on contract', 'in writing', 'word for word', 'out to tender', 'at fault', 'on sight', 'on its face', 'in the same breath') are the correct bare forms, and the three rebuilt q5 options carry their determiners ('A crossing', 'A reliability figure', 'a set of', 'a dispute', 'The punctuality clause', 'the argument'). TENSE / ASPECT: the system is exact – present perfect for the standing record ('has taken it in twenty-three', 'has gone from thirty-nine minutes to fifty-four'), simple past for dated events, past perfect for the anterior ('the highest it had ever been', 'the interval had already gone from twenty-five to thirty-two'), futurate 'goes out to tender in the spring', characterising 'She will concede'. In the option layer q3-D's ellipsis 'than the timetable changes had' is a licensed past perfect (2013 precedes 2016) and q3-A's new 'It came before the first minutes were put on the book' is right in the simple past. Backshift in the new q5 rationale is correct: 'she would stand behind them in any room' reporting 'I’d stand behind them'. NEGATIVE POLARITY, every item licensed: 'Pad the book by nothing at all', 'does not accept that it caused any of this', 'before anyone was measuring', 'declines to grant the timetable any of the fifteen minutes', 'and no passenger at all' (licensed by 'no'), 'none of them can be discarded', 'The text is having no such argument', 'nobody has timed it', 'it was never a live reading', 'Neither record is in doubt', 'neither refutes nor ranks'. No orphaned NPI. RELATIVE PRONOUNS FOR NON-PERSONS: correct throughout. 'that' or zero on inanimates ('a sailing that does not run', 'the July draft that carries', 'the line that baits this option', 'the quarter that lost forty-one sailings'), 'which' only non-restrictively ('loading, which took longer then than it does now'), 'who' only on people ('the passengers who were not consulted', 'a reader who knows the field', 'the writer, who goes further than she does'), and q5-D's 'A ferry whose punctuality record has improved' – 'whose' on an inanimate is standard English and is the right choice here. ZERO RELATIVES WITH NO GAP: this was the r3 kill class and it is CLEAN. All thirteen zero relatives in the unit bind a gap; the offending string is absent from every live layer; and the four zero relatives inside fleet-repair-3's new q5 rationale ('the grievance a reader supplies unprompted', 'the argument the text is having', 'a limb the text supports', 'a limb the text refuses') each have one. PRONOUNS REACHING PAST INTERVENING REFERENTS: the r3 major and the r3 q3 minor are both gone. Two candidates were examined and both clear. 'and that silence, rather than any difference of confidence, is what separates it from D' – 'it' is A at twenty-four words, but 'separates X from D' forces X to be an option letter and the competing NP 'that silence' is already the subject, so the reach is licensed, unlike the r3 case where 'it' opened a new clause after a semicolon with no structural licensor. 'and paragraph 5 refutes it in terms' – 'it' is option C at thirteen words; the only competitor, 'Cottam’s position', converges on the same content because the dash-gloss between them defines the overgeneralisation. Neither convicted. MIXED COMPARISONS: none – both arms present in 'allowed less time for the crossing than the boat was taking', 'costs everyone not on it far more than the nine minutes cost the boat', 'removed more departures from the day than the timetable changes had', 'took longer then than it does now', 'more to do with the linkspan than with the certificate', 'booked slower than it was', 'her minutes show little and her explanation still less', 'goes further than she does'. COMMA SPLICES: none. The r3 splice is gone, and the two long comma-runs are serial coordinations closing on 'and'. GARDEN PATHS: swept for phrasal-verb readings available where none is meant. The consultation sentence ends on 'go' so no 'go above/go ahead' reading is reachable; 'arithmetic the text supplies but never adds up' keeps the transitive reading through the shared object gap; 'wave through', 'pull them apart', 'take apart', 'leaves the count altogether' and 'ran out' are all unambiguous in place. The one hit is 'put the second boat off the run', convicted above. Grammatical and recoverable, so flag, not kill.
